final_message:
The bug doesn't reproduce at this checkout (6f37b07, which is 9.15.0). It does reproduce on the published 9.12.0, 9.13.0 and 9.14.0 releases.

**Why it doesn't show up here:** the checkout's history already has a commit titled "fix: unsafe report for `no-lonely-if` (#19087)" (9db5b15). It's very likely the fix for this report. I didn't open its diff or the PR, since you asked me not to look at how this was resolved. Here, `lib/rules/no-lonely-if.js` checks `astUtils.areBracesNecessary(parent, sourceCode)` before reporting, so it doesn't report the inner `if` at all.

**The reproduction:** `repro-no-lonely-if.js` (repo root) lints and auto-fixes the snippet from the report with `Linter`. It then runs the code before and after the fix and fails if the result differs. It loads `./lib/api` by default, or any eslint path you pass as an argument.

Results with 9.12.0, 9.13.0 and 9.14.0 (all the same):
- It reports `3:9 no-lonely-if` with fix `{"range":[31,48],"text":"if (false) {}"}`.
- The fixed output is `else if (false) {}`. The outer `else throw ...` now attaches to that new `if`.
- Before the fix the code completes normally; after it, it throws "This `else` should have been unreachable!". The script exits 1 with `BUG: no-lonely-if autofix changed program behavior`.

With this checkout's `./lib/api` there's no report and no fix, so the script prints "OK" and exits 0.

**Cause, from 9.12.0's behaviour:** removing the braces pulls the inner `if` (which has no `else`) out of the block. The outer `else` then binds to it — the classic "dangling else" problem — and the rule never checks for that.

To see the bug, run: `npm i --prefix /tmp/eslint-9.12.0 eslint@9.12.0 && node repro-no-lonely-if.js /tmp/eslint-9.12.0/node_modules/eslint`. The patch only adds the script.

I also tried 7 variants against this checkout: deeper nesting, a loop or label between the two `if`s, a non-block consequent, and an inner `else`/`else if`. None of them gets an unsafe fix. The one variant that is still fixed (`else { if (c) {} else { if (d) {} } }`) keeps its meaning, because the `if` that comes out of the braces already has its own `else`.
